claude_take: The throughline today is scale outrunning consent. Alibaba and Tencent are throwing around trillion-parameter roadmaps, half-a-million-chip clusters and gigawatts of new data centers, while a few stories over, Pew finds a majority of Americans have turned against the very data centers making that scale possible. Even 'Coyote vs. Acme' only exists because public backlash forced a studio to reverse a spreadsheet decision, and a federal court just told the Capitol Police the same thing about the right to physically show up and object. Industry keeps betting bigger; the public keeps insisting it still gets a vote.

items.headline: Tencent Ships Hunyuan Image 3.5 Preview to Chase ByteDance and Alibaba
items.summary: Tencent released a preview of Hunyuan Image 3.5, merging image generation and editing into a single model with support for up to 20 reference images and native 4K output. The company's internal benchmarks claim rough parity with ByteDance's Seedream 5.0 Pro and an edge over Google's Nano Banana Pro, and the launch sent Tencent's Hong Kong shares up more than 6 percent. It underscores how fast China's image-generation race is moving, timed to land alongside Alibaba's Apsara conference.

items.headline: Alibaba Unveils Zhenwu V900 AI Chip and a 10-Trillion-Parameter Qwen Roadmap
items.summary: At its Apsara Conference, Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu introduced the Zhenwu V900 AI accelerator, three times more powerful than its predecessor and scalable to clusters of 500,000 chips, with mass production targeted for early 2027. Alibaba also confirmed Qwen 4 is already in training, with Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5 aiming for 5 to 10 trillion parameters, alongside a pledge to build 20 gigawatts of global data center capacity by 2032. The announcements sent Alibaba shares higher and mark one of the most aggressive infrastructure bets yet in the open-weight model race.

items.headline: Tom Cruise's 'Digger' Premieres in London, Splits Critics on Arrival
items.summary: Alejandro Iñárritu's awards-season contender 'Digger' had its world premiere as the Royal Film Performance in London's Leicester Square, with Prince William and Princess Kate in attendance. First reactions published the same day were sharply divided, with some critics calling it Cruise's best performance since 'Magnolia' and others dismissing it as a baffling misfire. The film opens internationally September 30 and in North America October 2, setting up one of the more contested Best Actor conversations of the season.

items.headline: 'Coyote vs. Acme,' Once Shelved as a Tax Write-Off, Crosses $100 Million
items.summary: The animated film Warner Bros. initially scrapped for a tax write-off, before public backlash forced a reversal and Ketchup Entertainment stepped in to release it, has now grossed more than $100 million worldwide, outperforming several of the studio's own 2026 theatrical releases. It heads to VOD on September 29, and its box-office run is reviving the question of whether it now qualifies for Best Animated Feature consideration. The turnaround has become a cautionary tale about studios writing off already-finished films.

items.headline: Pew: Americans Have Turned Sharply Against Data Centers Since January
items.summary: A new Pew Research survey of more than 10,500 US adults finds 54 percent now say data centers are mostly bad for the environment, up from 39 percent in January, and 50 percent say they raise home energy costs, up from 38 percent. Six in ten adults say they would be uncomfortable living near a new data center. The swing tracks the rapid, visible expansion of AI-driven data center construction and the wave of local opposition it has provoked across the country.

items.headline: Federal Appeals Court Strikes Down Capitol Police Limits on Protests
items.summary: The DC Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 2-1 that a Capitol Police Board rule barring public demonstrations on the Capitol's East Steps, unless sponsored by a member of Congress, violates the First Amendment. The case was brought by a minister denied a permit for a prayer vigil in 2021, and legal observers are reading the decision as a landmark expansion of protest rights at the Capitol. It lands amid separate litigation over the administration's press-access restrictions, adding to a broader pattern of courts pushing back on government limits on public expression.

items.headline: Donatella Versace Launches New Fashion and Beauty Venture With Revolve
items.summary: Donatella Versace is starting a new fashion and beauty brand as chief creative officer in a joint venture with digital retailer Revolve Group, her first major venture since stepping down as Versace's creative director in March 2025 after nearly three decades. The venture will launch beauty first, with the brand name and products revealed in the coming months and first products expected in 2027, targeting the US, Latin America, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East. It pairs legacy design authority with a digital-native retailer's data and audience reach.

items.headline: Experimental Wakefulness Drug Shows Early Promise for Adult ADHD
items.summary: Alkermes reported positive Phase 1b results for ALKS-7290, an orexin-2 receptor agonist that targets brain circuits governing wakefulness and reward rather than the dopamine and norepinephrine pathways stimulants like Adderall act on. In a 50-person proof-of-concept trial, two weeks of treatment produced dose-dependent symptom improvement on a standard ADHD rating scale, with generally mild side effects like insomnia and dizziness. It is the first clinical evidence that this drug class can treat ADHD at all, and a larger Phase 2 trial is now enrolling, though the results are company-reported and not yet peer-reviewed.

items.headline: Isaiah Berlin's Two Concepts of Liberty
items.headline_fr: Les deux concepts de liberté d'Isaiah Berlin
items.summary: In his 1958 lecture, philosopher Isaiah Berlin distinguished between negative liberty, freedom from interference by others, and positive liberty, the capacity to be one's own master and act on one's own reasons. He warned that positive liberty in particular could be twisted to justify coercion in the name of someone's 'true' or 'higher' self, a pattern he saw in the totalitarian ideologies of his century. The distinction remains a foundational tool for untangling arguments about freedom, whether the debate is about government regulation, platform moderation, or paternalistic policy.
items.summary_fr: Dans sa conférence de 1958, le philosophe Isaiah Berlin distingue la liberté négative, l'absence d'interférence d'autrui, de la liberté positive, la capacité d'être maître de soi-même et d'agir selon ses propres raisons. Il met en garde contre la liberté positive, qui selon lui peut être détournée pour justifier la coercition au nom d'un moi véritable ou supérieur, un schéma qu'il observait dans les idéologies totalitaires de son siècle. Cette distinction demeure un outil fondamental pour démêler les débats sur la liberté, qu'il s'agisse de régulation étatique, de modération des plateformes ou de politiques paternalistes.
